value.body: An instructor rating, issued by DGCA and endorsed on a pilot's licence, allows a pilot to teach student pilots at a flying training organisation. Pilots usually start with an Assistant Flight Instructor rating and move to a full Flight Instructor rating with experience. Many new commercial pilots instruct to build flying hours while waiting for airline jobs.

items.label: Ratings
items.note: Requirements are set in DGCA's rules for instructor ratings

items.label: Issuing authority
items.note: Ratings must be kept current through checks and recency

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Hold a CPL, complete an instructor rating course with a DGCA-approved flying training organisation (ground and flight training on teaching), pass the DGCA knowledge requirements and a skill test, then apply for the rating. Check the current DGCA civil aviation requirements for hour and experience thresholds.

value.title: At a glance
items: The course is an added cost beyond CPL training; fees vary by school and aircraft.
Instructing builds hours and teaching skills, but instructor jobs are limited to flying schools.
Some pilots instruct for a few years before joining an airline or charter operator.
